GOVERN — thin low-risk approval fatigue within named scope and with an explicit opt-out (standing-approval-and-auto-advance; never covers a protected-branch merge or arming auto-merge, which stay human-only); when the platform auto-deploys on merge, treat PR validation as the authoritative gate and keep a revert path (merge-is-deploy-governance); use a reusable operator prompt with stop conditions, backup-then-verify and evidence-based ETAs (gated-deployment-prompt-template). CURATE — choose and bound information sent to a model, keep a record of inclusions/exclusions that affect the result, minimize secrets/PII, make what the model saw reconstructible, design exclusions; nothing downstream trusts model output until parse -> strict schema -> policy scan, failures logged as safety evidence and rejected, never silently repaired; pin the curated input diet and output contract by eval cases.
